title: Design a Queryless Home Ranker
prompt: A guest has supplied trip dates, party size, location, and filters. You receive an eligible set of homes. Design a model to rank them without a text query. Discuss the objective, data, serving, and evaluation. How would you investigate a drop in bookings?

response.placeholder: Start with the ranking decision and a measurable booking outcome, then trace the data and serving paths.
response.reference_answer:
The source supports the task theme. The design below is a reconstructed practice answer, not a verbatim interview solution.

## Contract and objective

Rank only homes already eligible for the requested dates, guests, location, and hard filters. Optimize a downstream outcome such as completed bookings per search session while watching cancellations, guest/host satisfaction, diversity, and latency. Clarify whether the surface is a search-results page or a recommendation feed, and what personal history may be used.

## Training data and features

Log eligible candidate sets, impressions, positions, clicks, requests, bookings, cancellations, and ranking-policy versions. A booking is delayed; build point-in-time training examples with mature labels and avoid features recorded after impression. Use trip context, listing quality, price relative to local alternatives, location, availability freshness, and permitted user history. A new guest gets context and regional priors; a new listing gets content and host priors rather than a permanent cold-start penalty.

Start with a transparent rules or tabular baseline, then train a pointwise or pairwise ranker. Logged clicks and bookings are biased by prior exposure and position. Randomized exploration with logged propensities can support off-policy checks; otherwise treat offline comparisons as directional. Keep candidate generation and eligibility fixed during ranker comparisons so their changes do not masquerade as model gains.

## Serving and evaluation

Fetch time-valid features for the eligible candidates, score a bounded set, and return a stable ordered list within a latency budget. Cache only features whose freshness and guest scope allow it. If ranking fails, use a deterministic quality/popularity order while preserving hard eligibility. Evaluate NDCG or pairwise ordering on judged or mature outcomes, calibration, and cold-start/geography slices, then run an online experiment on completed bookings with cancellations, diversity, and tail latency as guardrails.

## Debugging

When booking falls, first separate shifts in eligible candidates or supply from feature freshness, model version, and score distribution. Compare slices by trip type, geography, new users, and new listings; inspect exposure and booking-label delays. Replay a small sample with logged candidate/features/model versions, and roll back the ranker if the experiment or guardrails show harm.
